problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y+4z=-2 \\ x+3y+9z=0 \\ y+6z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}9 & -8 & 6 \\ -6 & 6 & -5 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-3y+z=-1 \\ x-y+3z=2 \\ -2x+y-z=1\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, and the inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -8 \\ -5 & 0 & -5 \\ -1 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

the solution of the system of equations is 

$x=$
{{field-1}}, 
$\,y=$
{{field-2}}, 
$\,z=$
{{field-3}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -8 \\ -5 & 0 & -5 \\ -1 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 0 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is 

$$
x=-1,\,y=0,\,z=1.
$$
